adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving the level directly leaves notifications_reason_id nil, so a later read can auto-track the topic and silently undo the unsubscribe.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the unsubscribe action in topics_controller.rb lines 97-116, the code modifies tu.notification_level and calls tu.save!, but it never sets notifications_reason_id. The TopicUser model likely uses notifications_reason_id to track why a notification level was set. If this field remains nil or retains an old value, other parts of the system that auto-track topics based on user activity could potentially override the manually set notification level, effectively undoing the unsubscribe. This is a plausible bug in the business logic where the unsubscribe action doesn't fully record the user's intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440 — A state-changing unsubscribe is exposed as GET, allowing link prefetchers or cross-site requests with the user's cookies to alter notification settings without confirmation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in config/routes.rb line 440: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. The unsubscribe action in topics_controller.rb modifies the user's notification_level (tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!) - this is a state-changing operation exposed via GET. This is a security vulnerability because link prefetchers, browser preloading, or CSRF attacks could trigger unsubscription without user intent. State-changing operations should use POST/PUT/DELETE with CSRF protection, not GET.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:178 — The updated test supplies unsubscribe_url but only asserts the old preferences URL, so omission or corruption of the new per-topic link passes silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the test at line 171 now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the MessageBuilder, but the only assertion shown (line 175) checks for 'List-Unsubscribe' header presence. The new unsubscribe_url feature is being added (seen in user_notifications.rb passing unsubscribe_url, and server.en.yml adding the template text with %{unsubscribe_url}), but the test doesn't verify that this URL actually appears in the generated email content. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality - the test should verify the per-topic unsubscribe link is included in the output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440 — Exposing the state-changing unsubscribe action as GET lets mail scanners, previews, and prefetchers alter notification settings without user intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in config/routes.rb line 440: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. The unsubscribe action in topics_controller.rb modifies the TopicUser notification_level and calls tu.save!, which is a state-changing operation. Using GET for state-changing operations is a security issue because email scanners, link prefetchers, and preview tools can trigger these requests without user intent, potentially unsubscribing users from topics they didn't intend to unsubscribe from.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295 — The emailed URL carries no recipient identity or token, so it unsubscribes whichever account is currently signed into the browser instead of reliably unsubscribing the message recipient.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` is passed to the email (line 295 in user_notifications.rb), and `unsubscribe_url` is defined in topic.rb as simply `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` with no user-specific token or identifier. The unsubscribe controller action in topics_controller.rb uses `current_user` to determine who to unsubscribe, meaning whoever is logged into the browser when clicking the link gets unsubscribed, not necessarily the email recipient. This is a real security/correctness bug - the unsubscribe link should contain a token to identify the intended recipient.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — Adding required unsubscribe_url interpolation breaks existing MessageBuilder callers that set add_unsubscribe_link without supplying the new undocumented option.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that config/locales/server.en.yml now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation in the unsubscribe_link text. In lib/email/message_builder.rb, the code calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` to generate the unsubscribe link. The template_args are built from @opts, and unsubscribe_url is only added when explicitly passed (as shown in user_notifications.rb where it's now passed). However, existing callers that set add_unsubscribe_link: true without providing unsubscribe_url will cause the I18n interpolation to fail or produce broken output with a literal %{unsubscribe_url} in the email. The spec change confirms this - it now requires unsubscribe_url to be passed. This is a backward compatibility issue for existing callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving the level directly leaves `notifications_reason_id` unset, so reading the topic can auto-promote an unsubscribed user back to tracking and resume email notifications.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real issue in the unsubscribe action at lines 104-115. The code directly sets `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, but doesn't set `notifications_reason_id`. Looking at the TopicUser model's `update_last_read` method (lines 196-220), there's logic that auto-promotes notification levels based on conditions. Without setting `notifications_reason_id` to indicate the user explicitly chose this level, the auto-promotion logic could potentially override the user's unsubscribe choice when they read the topic again. This is a legitimate correctness concern where the unsubscribe action may not persist as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — The action dereferences a missing `TopicUser`, so a logged-in user without an existing topic-user row gets a 500 instead of being muted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the unsubscribe action in topics_controller.rb lines 97-115, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately accesses `tu.notification_level` without checking if `tu` is nil. If a logged-in user visits the unsubscribe URL for a topic they've never interacted with (no TopicUser record exists), `find_by` returns nil, and `tu.notification_level` will raise a NoMethodError (nil has no method notification_level), resulting in a 500 error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440 — Unsubscribing is performed by a GET request, allowing authenticated prefetches or cross-site requests to change notification state without user intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in config/routes.rb lines 440-441 that the unsubscribe endpoint is defined as a GET route: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`. The controller action in topics_controller.rb modifies the TopicUser notification_level and calls `tu.save!`. This is a state-changing operation performed via GET request, which violates HTTP semantics and is vulnerable to CSRF attacks, link prefetching, and accidental triggering. The finding correctly identifies this security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — A state-changing GET without a CSRF token lets an attacker force an authenticated user to alter per-topic notification settings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb that modifies TopicUser notification_level state. It's added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 27) and the route is defined as a GET request (config/routes.rb shows `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). This is a state-changing operation (tu.notification_level modification and tu.save!) on a GET request without CSRF protection, which could allow an attacker to craft a link that changes a user's notification settings when clicked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:178 — The updated test supplies unsubscribe_url but asserts only the pre-existing preferences URL, so omission or corruption of the new per-topic link would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the test at line 171-172 was updated to include 'unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"' in the message builder options. However, looking at the test assertion at line 175, it only checks 'expect(message_with_unsubscribe.header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present' - this verifies the header exists but doesn't verify the new unsubscribe_url is actually used or included correctly. The finding correctly identifies that the test doesn't adequately verify the new per-topic unsubscribe URL functionality that was added. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for new functionality, making it an important non-bug issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — The new state-changing endpoint has no request coverage for authentication, canonical redirects, notification-level transitions, or missing TopicUser records.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb lacks test coverage. Looking at the diff, the action is added to `ensure_logged_in` (line 27-28) and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 32), but the spec file changes only show tests for MessageBuilder, not for the new controller action. The action has several edge cases: it handles slug redirects, modifies TopicUser notification levels with specific transition logic (regular->muted or higher->regular), and calls `tu.save!` which could fail if TopicUser doesn't exist. The finding about missing test coverage for this new nontrivial logic is valid and specific to the diff.
